Subject: Re: Quick post-demo notes

Diego —

Thanks for the demo earlier. High level takeaways from our side: Stratos needs predictable 95th pct latency under 300ms for chat use cases, and we have strict hallucination constraints on knowledge-intensive prompts. We want to see a head-to-head against our current hyperscaler endpoint (CloudLarge) across the 5 probe classes we discussed.

Can you send a short plan for what tests/redlines you would run next and what artifacts you’ll share? Also, we need to understand fallback behavior if Redwood-serving variant fails for a particular prompt.

Appreciate a concise plan — Sam

--
Sam Hughes
Head of Platform
Stratos Systems
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example>
To: Sam Hughes <sam.hughes@stratos.ai>, Aisha Khan <aisha.k@stratos.ai>, Jared Park <jared.park@stratos.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo notes

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Short plan below (keeping it tight so you can share with procurement/eng):

1) What we’ll run (deliverables)
- Small probe suite (5 classes): knowledge-grounded Qs, multi-step reasoning, entity-heavy extraction, instruction-following with constraints, and conversational context continuity. Prompt set attached as stratos_eval_prompt_set_v2.csv.
- Side-by-side metrics vs CloudLarge (their API) and your current baseline: 95th/99th latency, P50, per-prompt hallucination flag rate, confidence calibration, and top-1 token mismatch. We'll return a concise table (redwood_vs_hyperscaler_latency_table.xlsx).
- Representative failure / fallback traces for any prompts that trigger model-degradation + our automatic fallback behavior description.

2) How we’ll run it
- Controlled replay: we’ll replay your production-like trace (you can scrub PII) or use the attached probe set. Tests run on our Dedicated cluster to match latency targets.
- Per-prompt concurrency sweep: low (1) / medium (8) / high (64) concurrency to show throughput/latency tradeoffs and batching effects.

3) Hallucination probes and regression checks
- We’ll run the hallucination_probe_examples.txt (sample flagged cases) and compute per-class hallucination_rate and a short human-audit of ~30 edge cases.
- Regression check: run your historical prompt snapshot vs current Redwood-optimized runtime and a quantized variant we propose.

4) Fallback behavior
- Default: route to high-consistency variant (larger model/FP16) if quality threshold fails.
- If dedicated capacity unavailable, route to hosted variant in a different region and return warning header in response. We’ll attach example traces in the report.

5) Timeline & next steps
- Run a quick pilot (non-prod) within 3 business days after you approve the probe set.
- Deliverables: results summary + artifact package within 5 business days of pilot start.

If that plan looks good I’ll kick off the pilot and schedule a 30-min alignment call (engineers + platform) next week.

Thanks — Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@stratos.ai>

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo notes

Diego — this looks exactly like what we need. Two quick clarifications before we approve the probe set: 1) For hallucination_rate do you use human annotation or automated heuristics? 2) For the fallback, will we be able to configure a hard fail vs. soft degrade?

Also can you include a short note on token accounting for the different fallback paths (cost delta)? We need that for procurement.

If you can answer by EOD PST, we’ll greenlight the pilot.

Thanks,
Aisha
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@stratos.ai>, Sam Hughes <sam.hughes@stratos.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo notes

Aisha — great questions. Quick answers inline: 

1) Hallucination measurement
- Primary: automated classifiers (precision-oriented) to surface likely hallucinations across the full probe set; secondary: human annotation on a stratified sample of ~30 edge cases to validate false positives/negatives and compute the final reported hallucination_rate. We’ll include both numbers (automated vs human-audited).

2) Fallback config
- Yes — configurable. We expose two modes in the rollout policy: HARD_FAIL (return an explicit 5xx and trigger on-call) or SOFT_DEGRADE (automatically route to higher-consistency variant and annotate response with X-Redwood-Fallback header). We’ll document default behavior and how to change it per-route.

3) Token accounting / cost delta
- We’ll produce a short table showing per-prompt token consumption across (a) CloudLarge baseline, (b) Redwood-hosted optimized, (c) Redwood-dedicated with quantization. Early estimate: dedicated + quantization reduces per-token ops cost ~18-26% depending on prompt length; exact $ delta in the spreadsheet we’ll send.

Next steps
- We’ll upload the probe set and cost/latency tables to the Drive folder linked above and start the pilot once you confirm.
- Proposed alignment call: Wed 05/12 10:00am PT — Diego, Marissa (SWE), Laura (AM), and your Eng/Platform rep. Does that slot work?

Attaching: stratos_eval_prompt_set_v2.csv; hallucination_probe_examples.txt; redwood_vs_hyperscaler_latency_table.xlsx (stubs)

Diego
